rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many tafsirs depend on earlier works, differing chiefly in how briefly or expansively they collect material.
rows.anchor: سابق بحيث لاحظ لمؤلفه إلا الجمع على تفاوت بين اختصار وتطويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He names al-Kashshaf, Ibn Atiyya’s al-Muharrar al-Wajiz, al-Razi’s Mafatih al-Ghayb, al-Baydawi, and al-Alusi among the leading commentaries.
rows.anchor: وإن أهم التفاسير تفسير الكشاف و المحرر الوجيز لابن عطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His list also includes commentaries on al-Kashshaf and al-Baydawi, Abu al-Suud, al-Qurtubi, legal tafsirs, al-Tabari, and Durra al-Tanzil, attributed to al-Razi or perhaps al-Raghib.
rows.anchor: وتفسير الشهاب الآلوسي ، وما كتبه الطيبي والقزويني والقطب والتفتزاني على الكشاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extant tafsir of Muhammad ibn Arfa is al-Ubbi’s student notes, closer to commentary on Ibn Atiyya than a complete tafsir, and it does not cover every verse.
rows.anchor: والموجود من تفسير الشيخ محمد بن عرفة التونسي من تقييد تلميذه الأبي وهو بكونه تعليقا على تفسير ابن عطية أشبه منه بالتفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For brevity, he generally omits attribution to the earlier commentaries he uses.
rows.anchor: ولقصد الاختصار أعرض عن العزو إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He distinguishes insights and scholarly questions he has not found in the tafsirs available to him on that particular verse, without claiming originality.
rows.anchor: وقد ميزت ما يفتح الله لي من فهم في معاني كتابه وما أجلبه من المسائل العلمية ، مما لا يذكره المفسرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He disclaims being the first to make an observation, since another thinker may have preceded him; he invokes the proverb about poets leaving no patch unstitched.
rows.anchor: ولست أدعي انفرادي به في نفس الأمر ، فكم من كلام تنشئه تجدك قد سبقك إليه متكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic meanings and aims are varied and far-reaching: rulings, manners, and stories appear in their relevant passages, while one verse may cover several themes.
rows.anchor: إن معاني القرآن ومقاصده ذات أفانين كثيرة بعيدة المدى مترامية الأطراف موزعة على آياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every verse contains subtleties of rhetoric, a Quranic art not given its own dedicated tafsir book as other subjects were.
rows.anchor: ولكن فنا من فنون القرآن لا تخلو عن دقائقه ونكته آية من آيات القرآن ، وهو فن دقائق البلاغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He undertakes to note rhetorical subtleties he perceives in each verse, according to his understanding and capacity for reflection.
rows.anchor: من أجل ذلك التزمت أن لا أغفل التنبيه على ما يلوح لي من هذا الفن العظيم في آية من آي القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tafsir emphasizes the Quran’s inimitability, Arabic rhetorical subtleties, and patterns of usage.
rows.anchor: وقد اهتممت في تفسيري هذا ببيان وجوه الإعجاز ونكت البلاغة العربية وأساليب الاستعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He examines links between successive verses; al-Razi attended to this, and al-Biqa‘i wrote Nizam al-Durar, but their treatments leave many verses insufficiently explained.
rows.anchor: واهتممت أيضا ببيان تناسب اتصال الآي بعضها ببعض ، وهو منزع جليل قد عني به فخر الدين الرازي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An exegete is not obliged to explain the coherence of the order of suras.
rows.anchor: أما البحث عن تناسب مواقع السور بعضها إثر بعض ، فلا أراه حقا على المفسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He outlines each sura’s aims so readers see the Quran’s harmony and beauty rather than treating its words and clauses as disconnected fragments.
rows.anchor: ولم أغادر سورة إلا بينت ما أحيط به من أغراضها لئلا يكون الناظر في تفسير القرآن مقصورا على بيان مفرداته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He carefully verifies Arabic lexical meanings and vocalization, including details missing from many dictionaries.
rows.anchor: واهتممت بتبيين معاني المفردات في اللغة العربية بضبط وتحقيق مما خلت عن ضبط كثير منه قواميس اللغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says he worked to uncover Quranic meanings, inimitability, and eloquent usage overlooked by prior tafsirs, hoping readers benefit according to their capacity.
rows.anchor: فإني بذلت الجهد في الكشف عن نكت من معاني القرآن وإعجازه خلت عنها التفاسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He presents the work as concise yet comparable to extensive commentaries, and titles it al-Tahrir wa-l-Tanwir, shortened from its full title.
rows.anchor: وسميته تحرير المعنى السديد ، وتنوير العقل الجديد ، من تفسير الكتاب المجيد . واختصرت هذا الاسم باسم التحرير والتنوير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sura names date from the revelation period and make reference and review easier; a report from Ibn Abbas says the Prophet directed each revealed verse to its sura.
rows.anchor: وقد دل حديث ابن عباس الذي ذكر آنفا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول إذا نزلت الآية وضعوها في السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of a sura name is to distinguish that sura from the others.
rows.anchor: وفائدة التسمية أن تكون بما يميز السورة عن غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Names may have developed from ‘the sura in which X is mentioned’ by dropping the relative clause and then the implied noun, or may directly affiliate the sura with a related subject.
rows.anchor: وأصل أسماء السور أن تكون بالوصف كقولهم السورة التي يذكر فيها كذا ، ثم شاع فحذفوا الموصول

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari transmits from Aisha an account associated with the revelation of the final verses of al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وقد ثبت في صحيح البخاري قول عائشة رضي الله عنها لما نزلت الآيات من آخر البقرة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A report in al-Bukhari says the Prophet recited al-Najm.
rows.anchor: وفيه عن ابن مسعود قال قرأ رسول الله النجم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet prostrated during al-Najm.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن رسول الله سجد بالنجم

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: A marfu‘ report attributed to Anas prohibits saying names such as Surat al-Baqara, Surat Aal Imran, or Surat al-Nisa, and directs people to say ‘the sura in which’.
rows.anchor: وما روى من حديث عن أنس مرفوعا لا تقولوا سورة البقرة ولا سورة آل عمران

rows.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
rows.claim: Ahmad ibn Hanbal grades the prohibition report as munkar.
rows.anchor: فقال أحمد بن حنبل هو حديث منكر

rows.speaker: ابن الجوزي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi includes the Anas report in his collection of fabricated reports.
rows.anchor: وذكره ابن الجوزي في الموضوعات

rows.speaker: ابن حجر
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar, by contrast, authenticates the report.
rows.anchor: ولكن ابن حجر أثبت صحته

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar is said to have used the same wording without attributing it to the Prophet; al-Bayhaqi records it in Shu‘ab al-Iman.
rows.anchor: ويذكر عن ابن عمر أنه كان يقول مثل ذلك ولا يرفعه إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الحجاج بن يوسف
rows.claim: Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf also forbade people to say ‘sura of X’ and ordered the longer descriptive form.
rows.anchor: وكان الحجاج بن يوسف يمنع من يقول سورة كذا ويقول قل السورة التي يذكر فيها كذا

rows.speaker: الذين صححوا حديث أنس
rows.claim: Those who authenticated the prohibition explain it as a Meccan response to mockery when Muslims used names such as al-Fil and al-Ankabut.
rows.anchor: والذين صححوا حديث أنس تأولوه وتأولوا قول ابن عمر بأن ذلك كان في مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It was reported that the mockery was the occasion for the revelation of 15:95; the author says migration removed the cause of the naming ban, which was then abrogated.
rows.anchor: فلما هاجر المسلمون إلى المدينة زال سبب النهي فنسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition did not become established practice; al-Bukhari’s chapter heading says there is no harm in naming suras, and its reports give examples including some wording from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ولهذا ترجم البخاري في كتاب فضائل القرآن بقوله باب من لم ير بأسا أن يقول سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The author permits both the descriptive name and forms such as Surat al-Najm, citing the several designations in Ibn Abbas’s prostration report.
rows.anchor: وعليه فللقائل أن يقول سورة البقرة أو التي يذكر فيها البقرة ، وأن يقول سورة والنجم وسورة النجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Companions apparently used names learned from the Prophet or familiar popular names; Ibn Masud’s naming of the two qunut suras al-Khal‘ and al-Hafd shows that some names were his own.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الصحابة سموا بما حفظوه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أو أخذوا لها أشهر الأسماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sura names can describe a quality, a distinctive subject, a person treated at length, or words occurring in the sura.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن أسماء السور إما أن تكون بأوصافها مثل الفاتحة وسورة الحمد ، وإما أن تكون بالإضافة لشيء اختصت بذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suras beginning with Ha Mim are collectively called Al-Hawamim; al-Kafirun and al-Ikhlas share the descriptive name al-Muqashqishatan.
rows.anchor: وقد سموا مجموع السور المفتتحة بكلمة حم آل حم وربما سموا السورتين بوصف واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Companions omitted sura titles from the codex to avoid inserting non-Quranic text, using the basmala to mark divisions because it suits openings and is itself Quran.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الصحابة لم يثبتوا في المصحف أسماء السور بل اكتفوا بإثبات البسملة في مبدأ كل سورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Itqan says al-Bayyina was called Surat Ahl al-Kitab in Ubayy’s codex, suggesting he did write sura names there.
rows.anchor: وفي الإتقان أن سورة البينة سميت في مصحف أبى سورة أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sura names were regularly written in codices during the Followers’ period without objection.
rows.anchor: وكتبت أسماء السور في المصاحف باطراد في عصر التابعين ولم ينكر عليهم

rows.speaker: المازري
rows.claim: Al-Maziri quotes al-Qadi Abu Bakr al-Baqillani: sura titles were written in a different script to distinguish them from Quran, while the basmala matched Quranic script.
rows.anchor: قال المازري في شرح البرهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Nahhas’s appeal to a report from Ibn Umar as proof that Quranic pause marks are obligatory is unclear; he refers readers to al-Suyuti’s al-Itqan.
rows.anchor: النحاس من الاحتجاج لوجوب ضبط أوقاف القرآن بكلام لعبد الله بن عمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They prioritized verse endings, whose challenge to the eloquent leaders among their people established the Quran’s proof against both those leaders and ordinary people.
rows.anchor: فكان الاعتبار بفواصله التي هي مقاطع آياته عندهم أهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As many ordinary Arabs and people from other nations entered Islam, scholars marked pauses to ease reading; they applied interpretive criteria, so a marker’s placement conveyed a proposed meaning.
rows.anchor: فلما كثر الداخلون في الإسلام من دهماء العرب ومن عموم بقية الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Notable authorities on pause marking include Ibn al-Anbari, Ibn al-Nahhas, al-Nakzawi (or al-Nakzwi), and the later Moroccan scholar Muhammad ibn Abi Jum‘a al-Hibti, who died in 930 AH.
rows.anchor: وأشهر من تصدى لضبط الوقوف أبو محمد بن الانباري ، وأبو جعفر بن النحاس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Differences in consonantal form include malik and maliki in ‘Master of the Day of Judgment.’
rows.anchor: يوم الدين ( و ) ملك يوم الدين (

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites nunshiruha and nunshizuha as another example of variants differing in letters.
rows.anchor: و ) ننشرها ( و ) ننشزها (

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites readings of qad kudhibu with the dhal doubled or lightened as a consonantal variant.
rows.anchor: بتشديد الذال أو ) قد كذبوا ( بتخفيفه

words: ولما ضرب ابن مريم مثلا إذا قومك منه يصدون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi reads yassuddun with the sad vowelled u, meaning they turn others away; Hamza reads yassiddun with i, meaning they themselves turn away; both behaviors occur among them.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع بضم الصاد وقرأ حمزة بكسر الصاد ، فالأولى بمعنى يصدون غيرهم عن الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Variants such as yathurna/yattahharna and lamastum/lamastum increase the possible meanings of a verse.
rows.anchor: نحو ) حتى يطهرن ( بفتح الطاء المشددة والهاء المشددة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also cites the variants ‘those who are with the All-Merciful are females’ and ‘servants of the All-Merciful’ as meaning-enriching readings.
rows.anchor: مع قراءة ) الذين هم عباد الرحمن (

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Variant readings are especially relevant to tafsir because one reading can clarify its counterpart or yield an additional meaning; different readings often expand a single verse’s meanings.
rows.anchor: وهي من هذه الجهة لها مزيد تعلق بالتفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He considers it likely that revelation came in both or more forms, if all well-known readings are accepted as transmitted from the Prophet, so the readings multiply meanings.
rows.anchor: والظن أن الوحي نزل بالوجهين وأكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Quranic wording may intentionally accommodate several readings, each adding meanings like multiple verses; he compares this to inclusion, double entendre, and implications of composition.
rows.anchor: على أنه لا مانع من أن يكون مجيء ألفاظ القرآن على ما يحتمل تلك الوجوه مرادا لله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Al-Farisi appears to prefer construing the reading with huwa so huwa is a pronoun of separation, since treating it as a subject would not explain its omission in Nafi and Ibn Amir’s reading.
rows.anchor: قد يؤخذ من كلام أبي علي الفارسي في كتاب الحجة

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects al-Farisi’s argument: readings need not have matching analyses, as different readings may each have a distinct grammatical direction.
rows.anchor: وما ذهب إليه ليس بشيء لأنه بني ذلك على توافق القراءتين

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan illustrates distinct readings with wada‘tu, ‘I know what I delivered,’ and wada‘at, ‘God knows what she delivered.’
rows.anchor: كقراءة ) والله أعلم بما وضعت (

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An exegete should explain the mutawatir readings because their differences usually expand the verse’s meanings, with multiple readings functioning like multiple Quranic words.
rows.anchor: وأنا أرى أن على المفسر أن يبين اختلاف القراءات المتواترة

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: In al-Bukhari, Umar reports that Hisham recited al-Furqan differently from what Umar had learned; the Prophet affirmed both recitations as revealed and said the Quran came down in seven ahruf.
rows.anchor: ففي صحيح البخاري أن عمر بن الخطاب قال

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Scholars address the difficulty in the seven-ahruf hadith through two approaches: some regard it as abrogated, others as still operative.
rows.anchor: وللعلماء في معناه أقوال يرجع إلى اعتبارين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stopping at a Quranic sentence ending can be essential to the meaning, which may change with pause placement.
rows.anchor: والوقف عند انتهاء جملة من جمل القرآن قد يكون أصلا لمعنى الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pausing at qutila means many prophets were killed by their enemies, while their companions did not lose heart; this consoles Muslims if the Prophet were killed in battle, as in 3:144.
rows.anchor: فإذا وقف عند كلمة قتل كان المعنى أن أنبياء كثيرين قتلهم قومهم وأعداؤهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Connecting qutila to kathir means many pious men were killed with the prophets, yet the survivors did not weaken, as in 3:169–170.
rows.anchor: وإذا وصل قوله قتل عند قوله كثير كان المعنى أن أنبياء كثيرين قتل معهم رجال من أهل التقوى

words: وما يعلم تأويله إلا الله والراسخون في العلم يقولون آمنا به
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stopping at illa Allah makes knowledge of the ambiguous verses exclusive to God, like knowledge of the Hour and the unseen matters; the following clause begins a new sentence about the learned entrusting it to God.
rows.anchor: فإذا وقف عند قوله ) إلا الله ( كان المعنى أن المتشابه

words: وما يعلم تأويله إلا الله والراسخون في العلم يقولون آمنا به
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joining illa Allah to what follows means those grounded in knowledge also know the interpretation of the ambiguous verses while affirming them.
rows.anchor: وإذا وصل قوله ) إلا الله ( بما بعده كان المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If one stops after ‘three months’ and begins anew with ‘those who have not menstruated,’ pregnant women would be coordinated with them, wrongly making delivery the term for women who have never menstruated.
rows.anchor: فإنه لو وقف على قوله ) ثلاثة أشهر (

rows.speaker: ابن الجزري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Jazari says no place in the Quran has a universally obligatory or forbidden stop; pause categories are graded by meaning.
rows.anchor: وعلى جميع التقادير لا تجد في القرآن مكانا يجب الوقف فيه ولا يحرم الوقف فيه كما قال ابن الجزري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stops are classified as emphatic, good, or lesser according to the meaning.
rows.anchor: ولكن الوقف ينقسم إلى أكيد حسن ودونه وكل ذلك تقسيم بحسب المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some scholars prefer stopping at completed speech and using a shorter pause when meaning calls for a break before completion.
rows.anchor: وبعضهم استحسن أن يكون الوقف عند نهاية الكلام وأن يكون ما يتطلب المعنى الوقف عليه قبل تمام المعنى سكتا

words: يخرجون الرسول وإياكم أن تؤمنوا بالله ربكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic context prevents a mistaken reading if one pauses after ‘the Messenger’: no competent speaker would take the following phrase, ending ‘your Lord,’ as a warning against belief in God.
rows.anchor: فنحو قوله تعالى ) يخرجون الرسول وإياكم أن تؤمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 79:27, the verse ends at banaha and the pause falls after al-sama’; even when connected, syntax prevents banaha from being heard as part of the alternative to the question.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قوله تعالى ) أأنتم أشد خلقا أم السماء بناها (

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Different stops at the two occurrences of qawarira yield different senses: the second may confirm literal glass, or express arrangement by category; min fiddatin then refers back to silver vessels.
rows.anchor: فإذا وقف على قواريرا ، الأول كان قواريرا الثاني تأكيدا لرفع احتمال المجاز في لفظ قواريرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Quran was revealed among Arabic speakers to be understood, its basic meanings were accessible to them; the challenge of inimitability concerns the special rhetorical abilities of their eloquent leaders.
rows.anchor: ولما كان القرآن مرادا منه فهم معانيه وإعجاز الجاحدين به وكان قد نزل بين أهل اللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rhetorical embellishment is one source of inimitability; verse endings resemble poetic rhymes and rhymed prose cadences and are intentional in Quranic composition, so ignoring them neglects their purpose.
rows.anchor: وكان من جملة طرق الإعجاز ما يرجع إلى محسنات الكلام من فن البديع ، ومن ذلك فواصل الآيات
